claims.statement: A justified identity differs from an assumed identity; a conceptual gap alone neither refutes nor establishes ontological identity.

claims.statement: Weak emergence here means complete physical grounding without a new basic experiential law; strong emergence adds irreducible properties or laws and can overlap property dualism.

claims.statement: Property dualism alone supplies no detachable subject or survival condition; instantiation can remain dependent on an organized physical substrate.

claims.statement: A closure-based exclusion argument needs sufficient physical causation, mental causal relevance and rejection of systematic independent overdetermination. Energy conservation alone is not that argument.

claims.statement: Chalmers considers phenomenal bonding promising but questions its nature, boundaries and compatibility with qualitative and structural explanation.

claims.statement: Kastrup proposes shared surrounding mentation and perception across dissociative boundaries to account for a common world outside individual volition.

claims.statement: Chalmers distinguishes cosmic idealism’s mental grounding of all concrete facts from generic cosmopsychism; identity and nonidentity versions face different individuation burdens.

claims.statement: Chalmers treats cognitive fragmentation as a candidate reply while stressing disanalogies and large introspective costs; he does not claim to solve constitution.

arguments.name: Identity and physical realization
premises: Experience and its causal relations require explanation.
A single property may be accessible through different concepts.
Empirical causal evidence can warrant identification if rivals are adequately excluded.
bridge_principles: B-T12-ID: concept difference need not imply property difference.
B-T12-WARRANT: an identity still needs evidence; physical closure cannot be assumed from correlation.
arguments.conclusion: Physical identity/grounding is a live explanatory strategy, not disproved by epistemic difference alone.
arguments.strongest_objection: The account may capture reporting or causal role without phenomenal character.
arguments.strongest_reply: Identity theorist denies two items remain to be bridged once identity is warranted; separate epistemic access need not add a property.
unresolved_issues: Does the identification capture the target?
What empirical/semantic premises warrant the identity?
Weak emergence needs a realization account and subject boundary.
arguments.construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

arguments.name: Experiential bases and subject constitution
premises: Suppose physical description leaves intrinsic role-realizers open.
Suppose experiential role-realizers jointly constitute ordinary subjects.
bridge_principles: B-T12-R: experience realizes physical roles rather than intervening from outside.
B-T12-COMB: base properties and relations sufficiently ground a bounded subject.
arguments.conclusion: Experiential bases could integrate phenomenality and causal roles without extra macro-level intervention.
arguments.strongest_objection: Microexperiences plus physics may not necessitate another subject; palette and structure constraints are distinct.
arguments.strongest_reply: The complete base can include phenomenal relations; informational rather than geometrical structure may matter. Inconceivability/impossibility is not established.
unresolved_issues: Specify relation and boundaries without arbitrary selection.
Conceivability-to-possibility standard must match its use against physicalism.
Emergent macroexperience changes the constitutive model and restores causal/law costs.
arguments.construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

arguments.name: Naturalistic property dualism and causal/epistemic cost
arguments.position: PL1, with PL2 and substance variants differentiated
premises: Suppose phenomenal reality is not wholly physically grounded.
Regular psychophysical principles could explain particular experiential distributions.
Basic properties and laws can be legitimate explanatory stopping points.
bridge_principles: B-T12-L: irreducibility warrants this law model only with additional grounding argument.
B-T12-EPI: law-based reliability/acquaintance can justify beliefs without experience causing physical reports (proposed reply, not established).
arguments.conclusion: A psychophysical-law model is a distinct serious alternative; it neither entails a separable person nor removes its epistemic burden.
arguments.strongest_objection: Under closure and no overdetermination, distinct experiential influence threatens exclusion; epiphenomenalism threatens experience-based knowledge/reporting.
arguments.strongest_reply: PL1 appeals to lawful tracking and direct acquaintance without extra physical effects; PL2 instead questions closure and proposes interaction laws. Neither reply is simply a conservation-law refutation.
unresolved_issues: Why this mapping rather than another?
Would a tracking account secure truth/justification or only matching reports?
Interaction/substance variants lack inspected direct defender/reply chains in this packet.
arguments.construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

arguments.name: Dissociated cosmic idealism
premises: Experience supplies a known kind of concrete reality.
Suppose a shared conscious ground supports mutually constrained private perspectives.
Suppose bodies/world are extrinsic appearances of those relations.
bridge_principles: B-T12-DISS: selective cognitive access must ground finite phenomenality, not just block communication.
B-T12-APP: an appearance relation must recover exact neural interventions and public regularities.
arguments.conclusion: The model offers a unified candidate explanation if dissociation, manifestation and law constraints are independently justified.
arguments.strongest_objection: An analogy to dissociation in embodied people does not establish cosmic subject division; calling brain activity an appearance can merely redescribe data.
arguments.strongest_reply: Distinguish inaccessible contents from nonexistent contents and causal impingement from shared cognitive access; formulate one lawful shared environment rather than personal wishing.
unresolved_issues: Cosmic extension of analogy and clinical premises unverified.
Organism-scale boundary needs noncircular criterion and edge cases.
Specific laws and mapping not derived; shared substrate not automatically shared perceptions.
arguments.construction_status: Project conditional reconstruction informed by cited original; not a quotation or additional independent observation.

arguments.name: Cosmic constitution versus plural idealism
premises: Suppose a whole can be ontologically prior to local structures.
An experiential whole might realize physical roles.
Human perspectives require either identity-with-modes or distinct grounded subjects.
bridge_principles: B-T12-WHOLE: physical holism alone does not select an experiential ground.
B-T12-SUBJ: shared bearer, shared type of reality and numerical identity are different claims.
arguments.conclusion: Whole-first models relocate constitution rather than automatically solving it; plural idealism need not entail one universal subject.
arguments.strongest_objection: One subject cannot be numerically identical to multiple mutually distinct subjects under ordinary identity logic.
arguments.strongest_reply: Identity version relativizes access to modes; nonidentity version posits constitutive dependence. Plural idealism permits multiple basic subjects with lawful coordination.
unresolved_issues: Nonidentity grounding needs a sufficient principle.
Plural coordination and basic intersubject relations carry separate costs.
